# domestic-ui

> domestic-ui is a design system built on native HTML, CSS custom properties and cascade layers. Link one stylesheet and plain semantic HTML gets its look in light and dark, with WCAG 2.2 AA as the accessibility baseline; theme it by overriding semantic tokens. It packages existing web standards and well-known patterns: nothing here is original.

To use it, link `css/domestic.css` (copy the `css/` folder or clone https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui). Plain semantic HTML then gets the full look with no classes. Each component exposes one `data-<component>` attribute whose value is space-separated words matched with `~=`, such as `data-button="primary small"`, never classes; state is carried by native attributes and ARIA (`disabled`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-busy`, `aria-invalid`). Layout primitives and utilities are classes (`.cluster`, `.grid`, `.stack`, `.visually-hidden`), tuned with custom properties. Theme only by overriding semantic `--dui-*` tokens; primitive tokens are internal and may change.

## Principles

- [Principles](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/index.md): domestic-ui packages existing web standards and well-known patterns.
- [Native element first](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/native-element-first.md): Use the HTML element that already has the semantics and behavior you need: <button>, <a href>, <dialog>, <details>, <label>, <fieldset>, <table>.
- [Agent-friendly by design](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/agent-friendly-by-design.md): Humans and coding agents should be able to write a whole view from this document alone.
- [Accessibility baseline: WCAG 2.2 AA](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md): Every example must pass, and every token pair is tested against, these criteria.
- [Cascade layers](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/cascade-layers.md): css/domestic.css declares the order once, before anything else (@layer on MDN, CSS Cascade 5).
- [Theming](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/theming.md): All tokens are custom properties on :root with the --dui- prefix.
- [Opinions we hold](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/opinions-we-hold.md): Each of these is a choice between valid options, not a standard.
- [Layout primitives](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/layout-primitives.md): Class: .stack, .cluster, .grid.
- [Tooling](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/tooling.md): npm test runs, in order, and fails if any step fails.

## Tokens

- [Tokens](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/index.md): The two tiers of domestic-ui design tokens: 158 custom properties with their light and dark values.
- [Primitive tokens](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/primitives.md): All 84 primitive tokens in css/tokens/primitives.css (internal), with resolved light and dark values.
- [Semantic tokens](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/semantic.md): All 74 semantic tokens in css/tokens/semantic.css (public theming API), with resolved light and dark values.

## Base

- [Base elements](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.md): Native HTML elements styled by the base layer, with no classes.
- [Visually hidden](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/utilities/visually-hidden.md): Hides content visually but keeps it in the accessibility tree.

## Layout

- [Layouts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/index.md): Layout primitives and planned page layouts of domestic-ui.
- [Cluster](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/cluster.md): An inline group that wraps onto new lines (buttons, tags, nav links).
- [Grid](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/grid.md): A responsive grid: as many columns as fit, each at least --grid-min wide, never wider than the container.
- [Stack](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/stack.md): Vertical flow with a consistent gap between children.

## Atoms

- [Atoms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.md): Every atom in domestic-ui.
- [Text helpers](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/text.md): Lead, small and muted text helpers from domestic-ui, with copyable markup.
- [Quiet link](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/link.md): A link that takes the surrounding text color and keeps its underline, for dense UI.
- [Buttons](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/button.md): Button variants, sizes, link buttons and honest disabled and loading states.
- [Form controls](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/controls.md): Native form controls as styled by the domestic-ui base layer, with copyable markup.
- [Switch](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/switch.md): An on/off switch built on a native checkbox with role switch, following the APG Switch pattern.
- [Field](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/field.md): Label, control, hint and error message wired with aria-describedby and aria-invalid.
- [Badge](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/badge.md): Inline status labels with tone variants that meet WCAG AA contrast.

## Patterns and guides

- [Patterns](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/index.md): Planned and available interface patterns, from site navigation to app shells, with the standard each one follows.
- Alerts: Coming in M3. Messages about status, from notices in the page to live alerts for important, time-sensitive changes. Follows [APG Alert pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/).
- Breadcrumb: Coming in M3. The path to the current page as an ordered list of links in a labelled `<nav>`. Follows [APG Breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/).
- Card: Coming in M3. A self-contained item, such as a product or an article teaser, on a raised surface. **Our choice:** No native element or APG pattern exists; an `<article>` with a heading, where the heading holds the one link, so the whole card is not one long link name.
- Dialog and drawer: Coming in M3. A modal `<dialog>`, either centered or as a drawer along one edge of the viewport. Follows [HTML `<dialog>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element), [APG Dialog (Modal) pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/).
- Disclosure: Coming in M3. A summary that shows or hides more content, built on `<details>` and `<summary>`. Follows [HTML `<details>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-details-element), [APG Disclosure pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/).
- Menu button: Coming in M3. A button that opens a menu of actions. Follows [APG Menu Button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/).
- Pagination: Coming in M3. Links to the pages of a long list of results. **Our choice:** No native element or APG pattern exists; a labelled `<nav>` with a list of links and `aria-current="page"` on the current one, as for breadcrumbs.
- Popover: Coming in M3. Content shown on top of the page from a button, with the `popover` attribute. Follows [HTML `popover` attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#the-popover-attribute), [MDN Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API).
- Search: Coming in M3. A search form in a `<search>` landmark with an `<input type="search">`. Follows [HTML `<search>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-search-element), [MDN `<input type="search">`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/search).
- Site navigation: Coming in M3. The main links of a site in a `<nav>` landmark, with the current page marked. Follows [HTML `<nav>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element), [APG Landmark regions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/), [APG Disclosure navigation example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/).
- Tabs: Coming in M3. Sections of content shown one at a time, chosen from a list of tabs. Follows [APG Tabs pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/).
- Toolbar: Coming in M3. A row of related controls that is one stop in the tab order. Follows [APG Toolbar pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/).
- Typeahead: Coming in M3. A text field that suggests values as you type, with `<datalist>` first and an APG combobox only where `<datalist>` falls short. Follows [HTML `<datalist>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-datalist-element), [APG Combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/).
- App shell: Coming in M3b. The frame of an application: header, primary sidebar, main content and an optional auxiliary sidebar. **Our choice:** No standard defines an app shell; it is the HTML landmarks `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<aside>` placed with CSS grid, with no wrapper elements of our own.
- Compact density: Coming in M3b. A compact density token that tightens spacing for data-heavy screens. **Our choice:** No standard exists for density; one semantic token override that tightens space while targets stay at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
- Dashboard: Coming in M3b. A grid of summary sections, each with a heading, that reflows to fit the screen. **Our choice:** No standard exists; a CSS grid of `<section>` elements, each with a heading, that reflows without media queries.
- Data table: Coming in M3b. Rows of records in a native `<table>` with a caption, header cells and optional sorting. Follows [HTML `<table>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#the-table-element), [APG Table pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/).
- Filter bar: Coming in M3b. A row of native form controls that narrows a list or table. **Our choice:** No standard exists; a `<form>` inside `<search>` with labelled native controls in a row that wraps, and the result count announced as a status message.
- Large forms: Coming in M3b. Long forms split into labelled groups, in one or more columns. Follows [HTML `<form>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#the-form-element), [HTML `<fieldset>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-fieldset-element).
- List-detail: Coming in M3b. A list of items beside the details of the selected one, stacked on narrow screens. **Our choice:** No standard exists; a list of links beside the detail region, placed with CSS grid, where each item is a real link so the browser's history and the URL keep working.
- Split: Coming in M3b. Two regions side by side at a set ratio, stacked on narrow screens. **Our choice:** No standard exists for a fixed split; two regions placed with CSS grid. A divider users can drag would follow the APG Window Splitter pattern.
- [Guides](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/guides/index.md): Step-by-step guides for building with domestic-ui.
- [From a simple site to an ERP app](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/guides/simple-site-to-erp-app.md): Five steps from a plain content page to a dense business application, and which parts of each step are available today.

## Demos

- [Demos](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/demos.md): Demo apps in demos/ that use domestic-ui, each with a link to its source on GitHub.
- [Accessibility checker](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/a11y): Checks the built demo apps the same way the repository checks `examples/`: Playwright with [axe](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core) (tags `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`), in light and dark, with every `<details>` opened and checked again.
- [Angular](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/angular): The dashboard and account settings views in Angular 22: standalone components, two routes (`''` and `'settings'`) with Angular Router, a `title` per route, and `routerLinkActive` with `ariaCurrentWhenActive="page"` for the current link.
- [Astro](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/astro): The dashboard and account settings views as two static Astro pages (`src/pages/index.astro` and `src/pages/settings.astro`) sharing `src/layouts/Base.astro`.
- [React](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/react): The dashboard and account settings views in React 19 with Vite, as a two-page [multi-page app](https://vite.dev/guide/build#multi-page-app) (`index.html` and `settings.html`).
- [Plain HTML](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/vanilla): The dashboard and account settings views as two static HTML files, with no build step.
